From: security@aurorahealth.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: auditor@secureaudit.io
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ scope question — EU data residency carve-out

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we prepare the CAIQ for our internal security review, we need a controls-level mapping that clarifies which CSA controls are met by Redwood’s hosted service versus features that require Private / Dedicated deployments.

Specifically:
- We need a spreadsheet mapping CAIQ question IDs to Redwood control owners and a short description of the evidence artifact (log sample, policy, diagram).
- For the EU carve-out (Aurora will keep PHI in eu-west-1 only), please flag controls where data residency or processing location changes the answer (e.g., key management, logging residency, subprocessors).
- We also need a small set of runtime log samples showing tenant scoping and keystore access (redacted is fine).

Target: can you provide a first-pass package by Monday, 31 May? If not, an interim reply with the mapping for the top 20 residency-sensitive controls would be great.

Attachments: none in this thread yet.

Regards,
Thomas Lane
Security Manager, Aurora Health
security@aurorahealth.com

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: security@aurorahealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, auditor@secureaudit.io
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ scope question — EU data residency carve-out

Thomas — thanks for the clear ask. We can deliver a CAIQ crosswalk and a small set of artifacts that specifically call out residency-sensitive controls. Plan below:

1) Deliverables by Monday, 31 May (first-pass):
   - CAIQ crosswalk (xlsx) mapping question ID -> control owner -> evidence stub -> residency impact note.
   - Data residency diagram (png) showing tenant routing and regional keystore boundaries.
   - 3 redacted runtime log samples showing token issuance, tenant id enforcement, and keystore access.

2) Owners:
   - I will own the crosswalk and evidence narrative.
   - Marissa (CS Ops) will coordinate artifact pulls and DocuSign access for any audit artifacts.
   - Rishi (Platform SRE) will provide the runtime log samples and a short note on how KV cache and routing preserve EU residency.

3) Questions where we might need clarification from Aurora:
   - Do you require cryptographic keys to be hosted in your KMS rather than Redwood-managed keys for the EU carve-out? (This affects KMS-related CAIQ answers.)
   - Is your definition of PHI scoped to provider identifiers + health records, or do you need Tenant-level export controls beyond that?

4) Attachments we will include in the first pass: redwood_caiq_crosswalk_v1.xlsx (stubbed), data_residency_diagram.png (stubbed), sample_runtime_logs.txt (redacted).

If the timeline is tight, we can push a minimal crosswalk today for the 20 top controls and add artifacts on Monday. Which would you prefer?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
